prompt: Which correctly applies the Decorator pattern to add logging to a DataService?
choices: class LoggingService extends DataService { @Override void save(String d) { log(d); super.save(d); } }
class DataService { static void log(String d) { System.out.println(d); } }
class DataService { void save(String d) { } void logAndSave(String d) { log(); save(d); } }
explanation: Decorator: implements the same interface as the wrapped object, holds a reference to it, and adds behavior before/after delegation. Option A uses inheritance (extends) — valid but breaks if DataService is final or has many methods. Option C adds a static method, not a decorator. Option D modifies the original class instead of decorating it.
